newsitem.title: THAILAND: Argentina, Thailand in trade, drug-fighting pacts.
newsitem.headline: Argentina, Thailand in trade, drug-fighting pacts.

text.p: Argentina and Thailand signed an economic pact on Wednesday and agreed to cooperate in fighting the drug trade, Thai officials said.

The trade deal, witnessed by Argentine President Carlos Menem and Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, covers goods and services, transportation, banking, telecommunications, agriculture and industry, the officials said.
It replaces a 1941 trade agreement and was signed by Argentine foreign minister Guido Di Tella and his Thai counterpart, Prachuab Chaiyasarn.

"The agreement will facilitate future bilateral contacts of trade officials in all fields and pave the way for possible free trade arrangements between the two countries after the year 2000," Varathep Rattanakorn, a Thai government spokesman said.
The two ministers also signed a memorandum of understanding on anti-narcotics cooperation, said Thai Foreign Ministry spokesman Thinakorn Kanasuth.
Menem, accompanied by 80 government and business officials, is on a three-day visit to Thailand. He is the second Argentine government leader to visit Thailand since 1961.
Argentina is Thailand's biggest trading partner in Latin America with bilateral trade worth about five billion baht ($192 million) in 1996.
Thailand imports mainly leather products, steel and animal feed ingredients from Argentina, and exports textiles, rubber and canned tuna to the country.
